evidence: Ran `python3 scripts/session_report.py > /tmp/sa/cost_check.jsonl`. It produced 247 rows, 140 with cost_usd null and 107 non-null. I streamed all 140 null transcripts, parsing each line as JSON. I counted lines with type "cost-state" and walked the keys, excluding message/content/input/toolUseResult subtrees, for any key containing "cost". I also ran a raw regex for `"...cost...":` keys over each whole file. Result: 0 cost-state lines and 0 cost-named keys in all 140 files. One null file contains the substring "cost-state", but only inside message text, not as a record type. I added 2 tests to tests/test_session_fields.py, and `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_session_fields.py` gives 6 passed. I re-ran the report after the change: 247 rows, 140 null. No code change was needed.
observations: case a = 140 (no cost-state line and no cost key). case b = 0. case c = 0. Key names found: none. The 107 non-null sessions parse correctly.
root_cause: No code bug. All 140 null sessions have no cost-state line in the transcript, so null is correct. session_fields does not skip or misread any cost data. Effort cost totals read low because 140 of 247 sessions (about 57%) have no cost data to sum. The report must state this.
verdict: pass
metrics: null before 140 of 247, null after 140 of 247 (unchanged, as expected)
claim: Null cost_usd on 140 of 247 sessions is a data gap. Those transcripts have no cost-state line and no cost-named field. Cost totals are a lower bound that covers only the 107 sessions with cost-state. scripts/session_fields.py is correct and unchanged.
